bull.b: Near-zero leverage and steadily growing equity give Intuitive durable financial flexibility. Strong cash and negligible debt support R&D, service infrastructure, buybacks and withstand cyclical capital constraints, reducing refinancing risk and enabling long-term investment in products and training.

A dominant recurring revenue base (instruments, accessories, service) creates predictable cash flows and high margins. This razor‑and‑blades model links growth to procedure volume and installed base, supporting durable free cash flow generation and operating leverage even if system placements fluctuate.

A growing installed base and double‑digit procedure growth sustain long-term consumable and service demand. More systems increase lock‑in, training benefits, network effects and cross‑selling of new product variants, underpinning recurring revenue and margin sustainability over multiple years.

bear.b: Weaker tendering, domestic competition and regulatory clearance delays in China threaten a major growth market. Persistent pricing pressure and slow product approvals can materially reduce international placements and limit upside from a region that historically drove outsized incremental unit growth.

If extended‑use instruments materially lower per‑procedure instrument spend, Intuitive's core razor‑and‑blades economics could deteriorate. Unquantified rollout and adoption timing add structural revenue and cash‑flow uncertainty, complicating medium‑term instrument and accessory revenue forecasts.

Broader adoption of GLP‑1 therapies can structurally reduce demand for certain higher‑margin surgical procedures, shifting case mix to lower‑revenue ops. Sustained changes in clinical pathways would compress instrument consumption per patient and pressure recurring revenue and average revenue per procedure.
